parallel.requirements: Recognized ESM `.mjs` output, local-only imports, manual `--a` parsing, Python repr formatting, flatten/chunk/partition/bucketize behavior, OMD/FrozenDict behavior, and executable probing requirements.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Parent explored behavior first, then split implementation into four child-owned scopes: foundation value/literal modules, iterutils, dictutils, and argparse plus entry script.
parallel.implementation: Children wrote disjoint files in `/output`: `pyvalues.mjs`, `pyliteral.mjs`, `iterutils.mjs`, `dictutils.mjs`, `argparse.mjs`, and `test19.mjs`; completed children relied on contract assumptions or scratch stubs for sibling interfaces.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The parent received a swarm result reporting three completed children and one aborted foundation child, but the parent was cancelled immediately and did not reconcile or run the assembled program before artifact capture.
parallel.verification: Verification remained fragmented: module-level `node --check` and scratch tests ran in children, while the entry child explicitly avoided running `test19.mjs` against sibling modules.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The foundation child did not finish verification or return a completed handoff; the run timed out, produced no final response, and the official evaluator failed the captured artifact 0/162.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same ESM, `.mjs`, no-external-dependency, manual argparse, black-box executable probing, and byte-for-byte output requirements, including big ints and many Python repr edge cases.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single main agent owned exploration, all module implementation, entry script assembly, integrated testing, and final reporting without delegation.
serial.implementation: The serial run wrote `pytypes.mjs`, `pyliteral.mjs`, `iterutils.mjs`, `dictutils.mjs`, `argparse.mjs`, and `test19.mjs`, using BigInt-aware value modeling and a hand-written literal parser.
serial.integration_and_delivery: All files were authored in one coherent implementation pass and then exercised together through `node /output/test19.mjs` comparisons before the final completion message.
serial.verification: The serial run ran 16 curated byte-for-byte comparisons, argument parsing checks, and 60 randomized nested literal comparisons against the executable, all reporting zero local failures.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The serial run completed normally with strong self-verification but the official evaluator still scored 0/162, so the residual defect is not isolated by the available trajectory evidence.

comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had shared-state assembly without final reconciliation after the child writes; serial integrated by construction and verified the joined artifact.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official evaluations make this a both-fail pair: parallel and serial each scored 0/162. The concrete process difference is nevertheless large. Parallel delegated interdependent modules and ended when the foundation child and parent were cancelled, leaving no completed foundation handoff or integrated whole-program verification. Serial completed a single-threaded implementation and ran extensive local comparisons, but the official evaluator still rejected it, so the evaluator result shows an unresolved ordinary implementation or benchmark mismatch rather than a discordant parallel-vs-serial pass difference.
parallel_contributors: The foundation child responsible for the value model and literal parser was cancelled before final verification or handoff.
The parent received an aborted-child swarm result and then stopped without resuming the child or running an integrated entrypoint comparison.
serial_contributors: Serial owned all modules in one trajectory and ran integrated comparisons against the executable.
Serial completed normally and returned a final summary, but its current official evaluation still failed all 162 cases.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Serial probed big integers and represented ints with BigInt, while the parallel foundation child was delegated a JS-number integer model and never completed verification.
Both official failures may reflect ordinary implementation gaps not fully exposed by the visible local tests; the available official summary does not identify a single failing assertion.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: parallel pattern is an adverse process contributor in a both-fail pair, not an exclusive root cause
